title: CML Monitoring: BCR-ABL1 on the International Scale
summary: Read BCR-ABL1 results on the International Scale as a log ladder (MMR = 0.1%), apply the ELN 2020 milestones at 3, 6 and 12 months, and judge whether an undetectable result has enough control transcripts to score deep response.

reviewer.note: Teaches Ch. 77 Hit 2 (first lesson for Ch. 77), with the ELN milestone table as context. Checked against Hochhaus 2020 (ELN) and Cross 2015 (deep molecular response scoring). Correction: the reviewer’s “MR2 = 10%” — ELN defines 1% IS as 2 logs below baseline (MR²); 10% is 1 log (rv-cml-mr2). Not taught: the reviewer’s “0.5–1 log rise on two consecutive samples triggers kinase-domain mutation testing” and the p210/p190/p230 isoforms (Hit 4) — not in the sources read.

objectives: Convert BCR-ABL1 IS percentages to log reductions and response categories.
Apply ELN 2020 milestones at 3, 6 and 12 months.
Judge whether an undetectable result has adequate sensitivity.

scenes.title: Is 0.08% good news?
scenes.altText: An invented CML patient on a tyrosine kinase inhibitor (TKI). BCR-ABL1 results on the International Scale (IS): 3 months 6%, 6 months 0.6%, 12 months 0.08%. A second report: “BCR-ABL1 not detected” with only 4,000 ABL1 control transcripts. Question token: “Which milestones were met — and does ‘not detected’ mean MR4.5?”

cues.text: A patient with chronic myeloid leukemia is on a tyrosine kinase inhibitor. BCR-ABL1 on the International Scale is 6 percent at 3 months, 0.6 percent at 6 months, and 0.08 percent at 12 months.
Another sample reports BCR-ABL1 not detected, but with only 4,000 ABL1 control transcripts.
Were the milestones met, and does not detected mean a deep molecular response?

scenes.title: The International Scale is a log ladder
scenes.altText: IS card (ELN 2020): molecular response is the ratio of BCR-ABL1 to a control gene (ABL1, or GUSB in some settings), expressed as % on the IS — a log scale anchored to the standardized IRIS baseline (100%). Ladder: 10% = 1 log below baseline; 1% = 2 logs (MR²; ≈ complete cytogenetic remission); 0.1% = 3 logs = major molecular response (MMR, MR³); 0.01% = 4 logs (MR⁴); 0.0032% = 4.5 logs (MR⁴·⁵); 0.001% = 5 logs (MR⁵). Schematic staircase, each step one log (×10) lower.

cues.text: Response is measured as BCR-ABL1 transcripts divided by a control gene, usually ABL1, and reported as a percentage on the International Scale.
The scale is logarithmic and anchored to a standardized baseline of 100 percent. Ten percent is one log below it; 1 percent is two logs, about equal to complete cytogenetic remission.
Zero point one percent is three logs: the major molecular response, MMR, also called MR3. Zero point zero one percent is MR4.
Zero point zero zero three two percent is MR4.5, and zero point zero zero one percent is MR5. Each whole step is a tenfold fall.

scenes.title: Milestones that decide treatment
scenes.altText: Milestone table (ELN 2020, BCR-ABL1 IS): 3 months — optimal ≤ 10%; warning > 10%; failure > 10% if confirmed within 1–3 months. 6 months — optimal ≤ 1%; warning > 1–10%; failure > 10%. 12 months — optimal ≤ 0.1% (MMR); warning > 0.1–1%; failure > 1%. Any time — optimal ≤ 0.1%; warning > 0.1–1% or loss of MMR; failure > 1%, resistance mutations, high-risk additional chromosome abnormalities. Back to the hook: 6% → 0.6% → 0.08% = optimal at every milestone.

cues.text: The 2020 European LeukemiaNet milestones decide whether treatment continues. At 3 months, 10 percent or less is optimal; above 10 percent, if confirmed, is failure.
At 6 months, 1 percent or less is optimal; above 10 percent is failure.
At 12 months, the target is major molecular response, 0.1 percent or less; above 1 percent is failure.
At any time, resistance mutations or high-risk additional chromosome abnormalities count as failure.
Our patient: 6, then 0.6, then 0.08 percent. Optimal at every milestone.

props.label: Any time: resistance mutations / high-risk ACA = failure

scenes.title: “Not detected” needs a denominator
scenes.altText: Sensitivity card (ELN 2020; Cross 2015): deep responses can only be scored if enough control transcripts were measured. Minimum control transcripts: MMR — 10,000 ABL1 (24,000 GUSB); MR⁴ — 10,000 ABL1; MR⁴·⁵ — 32,000 ABL1 (77,000 GUSB); MR⁵ — 100,000 ABL1 (240,000 GUSB). “Complete molecular response” should be replaced by “molecularly undetectable leukemia” with the number of control transcripts stated. Atypical transcripts card: 2–4% of patients have atypical BCR-ABL1 transcripts (e.g., e13a3, e14a3, e1a2, e19a2) that routine primers may miss → characterize the transcript at diagnosis; FISH monitoring may be needed. Back to the hook: “not detected” with 4,000 ABL1 transcripts cannot be called MR⁴ or MR⁴·⁵ — sensitivity is inadequate.

cues.text: A result of not detected only means something if enough control transcripts were counted. Scoring MR4 needs at least 10,000 ABL1 transcripts; MR4.5 needs 32,000; MR5 needs 100,000.
So the old term complete molecular response is replaced by molecularly undetectable leukemia, with the number of control transcripts stated.
Also, 2 to 4 percent of patients carry atypical BCR-ABL1 transcripts that routine primers can miss. Characterize the transcript at diagnosis; otherwise a false negative can look like a deep response.
For those patients, FISH monitoring may be needed.
Back to the second report: not detected with only 4,000 ABL1 transcripts cannot be scored as MR4 or MR4.5. The test was not sensitive enough.

props.label: 4,000 ABL1 → too few to score MR⁴

scenes.title: Three classic traps
scenes.altText: Three trap cards: “MR² = 10%” (✓ 1% IS is 2 logs below baseline; 10% is 1 log); “Undetectable BCR-ABL1 = complete molecular response” (✓ report as molecularly undetectable with the number of control transcripts; scoring depth needs ≥ 10,000/32,000/100,000 ABL1); “Any 3-month value above 10% is failure” (✓ > 10% at 3 months is failure only if confirmed within 1–3 months; otherwise a warning).

cues.text: Trap one: MR2 means 10 percent. No: on the International Scale, 1 percent is two logs below baseline; 10 percent is only one log.
Trap two: undetectable BCR-ABL1 means complete molecular response. Report it as molecularly undetectable, with the number of control transcripts, because depth depends on sensitivity.
Trap three: any 3-month result above 10 percent is failure. It is failure only when confirmed within 1 to 3 months; a single value is a warning.

scenes.title: The CML clock: 10–1–0.1
scenes.altText: Memory aid: “The CML clock reads 10–1–0.1 at 3–6–12.” And “MR-number = logs down: MR² = 1%, MR³ = 0.1%, MR⁴ = 0.01%.” Tokens: 3 mo ≤ 10% · 6 mo ≤ 1% · 12 mo ≤ 0.1%. A card lists where the aid breaks.

cues.text: Memory aid: the CML clock reads 10, 1, 0.1 at 3, 6 and 12 months. And the MR number equals the logs down: MR2 is 1 percent, MR3 is 0.1, MR4 is 0.01.
Where it breaks: MR4.5 is 0.0032 percent, not a whole log; warning zones sit between optimal and failure; and treatment-free remission and advanced phases have their own rules.

lines: Warning zones between optimal and failure

scenes.title: Takeaway
scenes.altText: Two tokens: “IS log ladder: 1% = MR² · 0.1% = MMR (MR³) · 0.01% = MR⁴ · 0.0032% = MR⁴·⁵ · milestones ≤ 10% / ≤ 1% / ≤ 0.1% at 3 / 6 / 12 months”, “Undetectable needs ≥ 10,000 / 32,000 / 100,000 ABL1 to score MR⁴ / MR⁴·⁵ / MR⁵ · atypical transcripts 2–4%”.

cues.text: BCR-ABL1 on the International Scale is a log ladder where 0.1 percent is major molecular response, milestones are 10, 1 and 0.1 percent at 3, 6 and 12 months, and an undetectable result is only as deep as its control-transcript count allows.

props.label: 1% = MR² · 0.1% = MMR · 0.01% = MR⁴ · milestones 10/1/0.1% at 3/6/12 mo
Undetectable: ≥ 10k / 32k / 100k ABL1 for MR⁴ / MR⁴·⁵ / MR⁵ · atypical 2–4%

explanation.what: Plain language: in chronic myeloid leukemia, a blood PCR test measures how much of the cancer’s fusion gene message remains compared with a normal control gene; results are on a shared international scale where each tenfold drop is one step, and treatment decisions depend on reaching set levels by set times. Scientific terms: BCR-ABL1, International Scale (IS), control gene (ABL1, GUSB), log reduction, major molecular response (MMR, MR³), deep molecular response (MR⁴, MR⁴·⁵, MR⁵), ELN milestones, atypical transcripts, molecularly undetectable leukemia.
explanation.why: Standardizing results to the IRIS baseline lets laboratories report comparable values. Because the scale is logarithmic, each response level is a tenfold change. Undetectable results depend on how many control transcripts were measured, which sets the lowest level that could have been detected.
explanation.measure: ELN 2020: 1%, 0.1%, 0.01%, 0.0032%, 0.001% = 2, 3, 4, 4.5, 5 logs below baseline; ≤ 1% ≈ CCyR; ≤ 0.1% = MMR (MR³). Milestones: 3 mo ≤ 10% optimal (> 10% failure if confirmed within 1–3 months); 6 mo ≤ 1% (> 10% failure); 12 mo ≤ 0.1% (> 1% failure). Minimum control transcripts: MMR/MR⁴ 10,000 ABL1; MR⁴·⁵ 32,000; MR⁵ 100,000. Atypical transcripts in 2–4%.
explanation.differs: MMR (0.1%, 3 logs) vs deep molecular response (MR⁴ and below); optimal vs warning vs failure; detectable result vs molecularly undetectable with adequate or inadequate sensitivity.
explanation.examAngle: Expect: the BCR-ABL1 % that defines MMR, log conversions, 3/6/12-month milestones, and whether an undetectable result can be scored as deep response.

comparisons.title: MMR vs MR⁴·⁵
comparisons.distinguisher: Depth of log reduction and the sensitivity needed to score it.

mnemonic.text: The CML clock reads 10–1–0.1 at 3–6–12; the MR number is the logs down.
mnemonic.explanation: Optimal: ≤ 10% at 3 months, ≤ 1% at 6, ≤ 0.1% at 12. MR² = 1%, MR³ = 0.1%, MR⁴ = 0.01%.
mnemonic.limitation: MR⁴·⁵ (0.0032%) is half a log; warning zones lie between optimal and failure; TFR and advanced phases have separate rules.

analogyLimitations: The patient and values are invented.
ELN 2020 is one guideline; other bodies’ milestones may differ.
takeaway: BCR-ABL1 on the International Scale is a log ladder where 0.1 percent is major molecular response, milestones are 10, 1 and 0.1 percent at 3, 6 and 12 months, and an undetectable result is only as deep as its control-transcript count allows.

questions.stem: Which BCR-ABL1 level on the International Scale defines major molecular response (MMR)?

options.rationale: Incorrect. ≤ 1% (2 logs) approximates complete cytogenetic remission.
Incorrect. ≤ 10% is the optimal 3-month milestone (1 log).

questions.stem: At 12 months of TKI therapy, BCR-ABL1 is 2% IS. How does ELN 2020 classify this?

options.rationale: Correct. At 12 months, > 1% is failure; > 0.1–1% is warning.

options.text: Cannot be classified without a bone marrow
options.rationale: Incorrect. Milestones are defined on blood qPCR results on the IS.

questions.stem: BCR-ABL1 is not detected in a sample in which 8,000 ABL1 transcripts were measured. What can be concluded?

options.text: The sample is not sensitive enough to score MR⁴ or deeper

options.rationale: Incorrect. That term should be avoided; depth depends on control-transcript count.

options.text: The patient has an atypical transcript
options.rationale: Incorrect. That is possible but cannot be concluded from this result; transcripts should be characterized at diagnosis.

accuracyFlags.issue: The reviewer states “MR2 = 10%” (and calls the ladder ~1.5 logs per step). ELN 2020 defines 1% IS as 2 logs below baseline and 10% as 1 log, and names MR³, MR⁴ and MR⁴·⁵ by their log reductions — so MR² is 1%, not 10%. See register flag rv-cml-mr2.
